what_is_cusma: [What is CUSMA?] Definition: CUSMA (Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement) is the successor to NAFTA. It allows Canadian employers to hire Mexican professionals without a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA).

[What is CUSMA?] Hiring Benefit: For an employer, this means the hiring process is fast, low-cost, and does not require proving that no Canadian could do the job. It is a streamlined visa process specifically for engineers and IT professionals.

frog_game: Frog Game Project Name: Frog Game (Android Mobile).
Frog Game Overview: An infinite arcade-style mobile game built in Unity 2D. The player controls a frog using complex touch gestures to catch insects while avoiding enemies.

Frog Game Architecture (Event-Driven): Implemented a decoupled Observer Pattern (Event System). Instead of rigid dependencies where the Player script calls the Game Manager directly, components broadcast events (e.g., `onEndingGame`, `onMovingFrog`). This prevents 'spaghetti code' and makes the system modular and easy to extend.

Frog Game Input Engineering: Developed a custom gesture recognition engine from scratch. Unlike standard button inputs, this system calculates the velocity and vector of the user's finger drag. A fast vertical swipe triggers a tongue attack (where swipe speed determines attack range), while horizontal swipes handle movement. Simple taps update the frog's facing direction.

Frog Game Performance Optimization: Initially built with standard `Instantiate`/`Destroy` methods for rapid prototyping. Arturo later refactored the entire spawn system to use **Object Pooling**, significantly reducing Garbage Collection spikes and ensuring smooth 60fps performance on mobile devices.

Frog Game Mechanics: Features include a Parallax scrolling background for depth, Coroutine-based animation timing for the tongue's extension/retraction (state management without blocking the main thread), and a dynamic 'Combo' system.
astar_pathfinding: A* Pathfinding Project Name: A* Pathfinding Visualizer (C# & Unity).

A* Pathfinding Overview: A custom implementation of the A* (A-Star) search algorithm built from scratch in C# within the Unity 2D engine. The project was designed as a computer science experiment to visualize how heuristic search algorithms navigate grid-based maps.

A* Pathfinding Algorithm Logic: Implemented the core A* loop using G (cost from start), H (heuristic cost to end), and F (total cost) scores. Arturo experimented with different heuristics, swapping between 'Manhattan Distance' (standard for 4-way grids) and 'Euclidean Distance' (better for the 8-way movement allowed in this project) to observe the impact on path naturalness.

A* Pathfinding Visualization Tools: Engineered a robust debugging suite (`AStarDebugger`) that instantiates visual indicators for every node in the open/closed sets. It renders real-time arrows pointing to parent nodes and displays raw F/G/H scores on the grid, allowing for a step-by-step visual audit of the algorithm's decision-making process.

A* Pathfinding Performance Analysis: While the initial implementation used a simple `HashSet` and LINQ-based sorting (`OrderBy`) to find the lowest-cost node, Arturo identified this as an O(N) bottleneck. He recognizes that for a scalable, production-grade RTS game, this should be refactored into a Binary Heap or Priority Queue to achieve O(log N) performance.

A* Pathfinding Unity Integration: Bridged the gap between Unity's physical world and the logical data grid using `camera.ScreenToWorldPoint` and `tileMap.WorldToCell`. This allowed users to dynamically paint 'walls' and 'water' tiles with mouse clicks, instantly triggering a path recalculation.

homelab: Project Name: Docker Homelab. This is an enterprise-grade self-hosting ecosystem.
Homelab Hardware: Running on a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (8GB RAM) booting from a high-speed MicroSD, with a 4TB SSD for persistent data storage.

Homelab Infrastructure: A fully containerized ecosystem using Docker and Docker Compose, managed via Portainer. The system orchestrates multiple interconnected microservices with strict resource limits.
Homelab Networking (VPN Sidecar): Architected a secure 'sidecar' network pattern using Gluetun within the Docker stack. Sensitive traffic is routed exclusively through an encrypted VPN tunnel.
Homelab Security (Kill Switch): If the VPN connection drops in the Homelab, the container's network interface locks down automatically, preventing any data leakage.

Homelab Engineering Challenge (DNS): Encountered a critical issue in the Homelab where the Docker daemon could not resolve registry URLs. Diagnosed it as a resolver conflict and fixed it by configuring a custom `/etc/docker/daemon.json` to enforce Google DNS (8.8.8.8).
Homelab Gaming: This Raspberry Pi also hosts a dedicated Terraria server (TShock) with automated world management.
Homelab Extras: The setup functions as a retro-gaming console (RetroPi) and a Steam Remote Play endpoint, allowing high-end PC gaming streaming to the living room TV.

Homelab Backups: Implemented a '3-2-1' backup strategy for the Homelab. Critical data is backed up locally to the SSD and encrypted (AES-256) before being uploaded to Google Drive nightly via Duplicati.
Homelab Observability: Deployed Glances for real-time system monitoring (CPU, I/O, Thermal performance) to ensure the Raspberry Pi stays within safe operating limits.
magicmail_dashboard: Cluster Dashboard Project Name: Email Cluster Administrative Dashboard PWA.

Cluster Dashboard Overview: A real-time, single-page application (SPA) built to visualize the health and status of the proprietary email cluster. It replaced a 12-page legacy interface with a single, unified view.

Cluster Dashboard Architecture (Real-Time): Built a high-performance frontend that consumes data from a custom C++ WebSocket server. The system handles 7 different data channels (System Overview, SMTP Stats, User Events, etc.) simultaneously.

Cluster Dashboard Frontend Engineering: Developed the entire frontend from scratch without using heavy frameworks like React or Vue. Instead, I built a custom component architecture using vanilla JavaScript, PHP for initial server-side rendering (SSR), and Sass modules for scoped styling. This 'Zero-Dependency' approach was chosen to ensure long-term maintainability within the legacy ecosystem.

Cluster Dashboard Networking Challenge (WebSocket Proxying): A major hurdle was configuring the WebSocket connection (`wss://`) in a strictly controlled ISP environment. The PWA requires SSL to function (Service Workers), but local development servers used self-signed certificates. I coordinated with the infrastructure team to provision valid SSL certificates and configured Apache to correctly proxy Secure WebSocket traffic to the internal C++ backend.

Cluster Dashboard Resilience (Exponential Backoff): Engineered a robust connection manager in JavaScript. If the WebSocket connection drops, the dashboard immediately enters a 'Reconnecting' state (showing loading spinners) and attempts to reconnect using an exponential backoff strategy (1s, 2s, 4s...) to prevent flooding the server during an outage.

Cluster Dashboard PWA & Push Notifications: Implemented a full Progressive Web App (PWA) implementation with a custom Service Worker (`sw.js`). This allows administrators to 'install' the dashboard on their devices. I also built a Push Notification system using VAPID keys to send critical server alerts (e.g., 'High Mail Queue') directly to admin devices, even when the browser is closed.

Cluster Dashboard Data Design: I defined the JSON schema contract between the C++ backend and the frontend. I negotiated a flexible data format with the C++ team that allowed for future scalability, ensuring the frontend could handle new data types (like 'System Events') without breaking existing charts.

Cluster Dashboard UI/UX: Designed a 'High-Density' information layout with dark/light mode theming using CSS Variables and Sass maps. The interface uses Chart.js for visualization and features a responsive grid layout that adapts from large control-room screens to mobile devices.
domain_health: Domain Health Project Name: Domain Health Dashboard.

Domain Health Overview: A proactive monitoring system designed to audit the health of domains hosted on the proprietary email platform. It runs automated checks (DNS, Registrar, etc.) to identify misconfigurations before they cause service interruptions.

Domain Health Architecture (Asynchronous Processing): Solved the 'long-running process' challenge by decoupling the scan execution from the user interface. Using PHP and AJAX, scans run in the background without locking the browser, allowing administrators to trigger audits on large domain lists and return later for results.

Domain Health Data Strategy (Last Known State): Implemented a 'Last Known State' persistence model. Instead of storing an infinite history of every scan, the database updates to reflect the most recent health status. This keeps the database performant while ensuring administrators always see the current operational reality.

Domain Health UX: Engineered a dashboard that categorizes complex technical errors into actionable groups (e.g., 'Missing A Record', 'Invalid TTL'), reducing the cognitive load for support staff trying to diagnose issues.
Domain Health Impact: Transformed domain troubleshooting from a reactive, manual process (waiting for a customer complaint) into a proactive, automated workflow.
mfa_system: MFA System Project Name: ClientID Mailbox Locking Interface.

MFA System Overview: A user-facing security dashboard designed to democratize access to an advanced 'Device Locking' (ClientID) backend. The feature allows non-technical users to restrict mailbox access exclusively to trusted devices, effectively blocking unauthorized login attempts even if passwords are compromised.

MFA System Architecture (State Machine): Designed a robust PHP-based state machine to manage a complex multi-step 'Wizard' workflow. The system enforces strict transitions between states (e.g., Unlocked, Device Selection, Confirmation Logic), ensuring users cannot skip critical security validation steps while registering their devices.

MFA System UX Challenge: The underlying security technology was powerful but 'unwieldy' for end-users. I engineered a simplified 'Click-to-Lock' experience that automatically detects the current browser's cookie signature ('Register Self') and presents a curated list of historical devices for approval.

MFA System Security Logic: Implemented MITM (Man-in-the-Middle) protection mechanisms including strict HTTP Referrer validation and session integrity checks to ensure the security interface itself could not be spoofed.

MFA System Impact: Transformed a complex, support-heavy server feature into a self-service product. This reduced the 'hand-holding' burden on ISP support teams and helped smaller ISPs meet cyber-insurance requirements for Multi-Factor Authentication.

MFA System Tech Stack: Built with PHP for server-side rendering, integrated with a proprietary C-based backend library via a custom wrapper, and uses Cookie-based device fingerprinting for identification.
dkim_manager: DKIM Manager Project Name: Self-Service DKIM Automation Module

DKIM Manager Overview: A security feature integrated into a proprietary email administration platform that allows administrators to manage DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) settings autonomously. This system reduced manual support tickets by automating the generation and deployment of cryptographic keys.

DKIM Manager Impact: Saved the support team approximately 6 hours per week by eliminating manual key generation requests. It empowered customers to secure their email domains immediately, removing the need for support intervention.

DKIM Manager Architecture (Distributed Sync): Engineered a cluster-aware synchronization system. Designed a scheduled asynchronous process to propagate DKIM configurations from the central management interface to all edge servers. This polling architecture ensured high reliability across the distributed infrastructure without introducing the complexity of a push-notification service.

DKIM Manager Security Engineering: Implemented a 'Least Privilege' access model to ensure the web application could generate cryptographic keys without requiring root access. The system supports both Global Keys (persistent) and Per-Domain Keys (rotatable), with built-in logic to safely handle key revocation.

DKIM Manager Legacy Integration Challenge: The feature required integration into a complex, pre-existing legacy framework. I performed deep architectural analysis to map the internal plugin structure, implemented the new feature seamlessly, and produced comprehensive documentation to aid future development.

DKIM Manager Business Logic: Implemented complex validation rules to ensure DKIM could only be enabled if strict pre-requisites (such as DNS record verification and domain ownership) were met, proactively preventing misconfiguration and email delivery failures.
